s: A company recently deployed an application on AWS. The application uses Amazon DynamoDB.The company measured the application load and configured the RCUs and WCUs on the DynamoDB table to match the expected peak load. The peak load occurs once a week for a 4-hour period and is double the average load. The application load is close to the average load tor the rest of the week. The access pattern includes many more writes to the table than reads of the table. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to minimize the cost of the table. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to increase capacity during the peak period. Purchase reserved RCUs and WCUs to match the average load.
Configure on-demand capacity mode for the table.
Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table. Reduce the provisioned read capacity to match the new peak load on the table.
Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table. Configure on-demand capacity mode for the table.
e: This solution meets the requirements by using Application Auto Scaling to automatically increase capacity during the peak period, which will handle the double the average load. And by purchasing reserved RCUs and WCUs to match the average load, it will minimize the cost of the table for the rest of the week when the load is close to the average.
x: Writes far outnumber reads, so DAX (a read cache) buys little, and on-demand costs more than provisioned capacity for a steady, known load. Reserved capacity for the average load plus Application Auto Scaling for the weekly peak is the cheapest.
